Finding under test (from analyst "broadcast-joins"):
{
 "id": "BJ-1",
 "dimension": "planning",
 "claim": "The FE's BROADCAST-vs-SHUFFLE decision is data-blind: with FILES() scans fixed at cardinality 1, the cost model reduces to (column type widths x alive-node count), so at 1 CN every join is BROADCAST (harmless, single destination) and at 4 CN the big joins flip to PARTITIONED and shuffle the LARGE table instead of broadcasting the small side.  "evidence": [
  "FE mechanism (measured in source): StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676 computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount=1, all columns UNKNOWN; Statistics.java:88-108 getOutputSize = sum(type widths) x 1; CostModel.java:401-432 BROADCAST cost = outputSize x aliveBackendNumber, SHUFFLE = outputSize; EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-322 checkBroadcastRowCountLimit never fires (rowCount 1 <= 15,000,000).",
  "survey/plan-summary.txt vs plan-summary-4cn.txt: q03 9:INNER JOIN BROADCAST build=orders -> 10:INNER JOIN (PARTITIONED) build=exch9<-orders probe=exch2<-lineitem; q10 13: BROADCAST build=lineitem -> 12:/15: PARTITIONED; q12/q14/q19 4: BROADCAST -> 5: PARTITIONED. Narrow build sides stay BROADCAST at 4 CN (q03 customer 4 B/row, q10 nation), matching the width-only cost.",
  "card-compare-cn4.txt actual rows shuffled: q03 exch2 lineitem 3,234,397,656 + exch9 orders 145,769,513; q10 exch8 lineitem 1,480,675,200 + exch5 customer 150,000,000; q12 exch1 orders 1,500,000,000 (to meet 31,162,904 lineitem rows); q19 exch4 lineitem 128,557,109 (to meet 2,158,428 part rows).",
  "cn4-transmits.txt bytes over nixl per query: q03 60.34 GB (58 GB is lineitem: 3 frames x 4.82-4.89 GB per CN), q10 48.04 GB (lineitem 26.6 + customer 19.2), q12 23.47 GB, q19 2.75 GB, q14 5.43 GB.",
  "Size of the small side that could be broadcast instead (parked bytes at 1 CN, cn1-ops.txt STREAMING_SINK/SOURCE input_GB): q03 orders x customer 2.33 GB (=> 3x2.33 = 7 GB traffic vs 60 GB); q10 orders-filtered 0.70 GB + lineitem x orders 2.29 GB (=> 9 GB vs 48 GB); q12 lineitem-filtered 0.51 GB (=> 1.5 GB vs 23.5 GB); q19 part-filtered 0.02 GB (=> 0.06 GB vs 2.75 GB); q14 lineitem-filtered 1.52 GB (=> 4.6 GB vs 5.4 GB, a wash).",
  "standalone/runs/q03,q10,q12.explain.txt: DuckDB (with parquet stats) builds on the same small sides the 1-CN FE plan broadcasts (orders x customer est 61.6M; lineitem x orders est 244M; lineitem-filtered est 244M).",
  "Measured wall cost of the shuffle at 4 CN (see BJ-2/BJ-3): q03 0.28 s/CN drain + 0.5 s arena dwell out of a 1.42 s span; 4-CN speed-up 1.93-2.14x (results-ratios.md)."
 ],
 "impact": "At 4 CN, 15-25% of q03/q10/q12 wall time is spent moving and staging the large table (drains alone: q03 0.28 s of 1.42 s, q10 0.24 s of 1.47 s, q12 0.12 s of 1.07 s) and the receive arena holds up to 88% of its capacity (BJ-3); at 1 CN the decision costs nothing. The FE's fragment cut is fixed before the engine sees any real cardinality, so neither the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism nor the translator can undo it (fact 11; node_translator.rs:1924-1931).",
 "confidence": "high",
 "code_refs": [
  "experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676",
  "experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/sql/optimizer/cost/CostModel.java:401-432",

  "experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/catalog/TableFunctionTable.java:188,300",
  "experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs:13-25"
 ],
 "queries": [
  "q03",
  "q10",
  "q12",
  "q19",
  "q14"
 ],
 "proposed_change": "Give computeFileScanNode a real outputRowCount for FILES() tables: cheapest is bytes-based (TableFunctionTable.fileStatuses already carries TBrokerFileStatus sizes: rows ~= sum(size)/estimated row width); exact is to return parquet num_rows from the CN's get_file_schema RPC (file_schema.rs already opens the footer). Even a row-count-only estimate re-arms checkBroadcastRowCountLimit (15M) and makes BROADCAST vs SHUFFLE cost proportional to actual sizes, so q03/q10/q12/q19 would broadcast the filtered small side and keep lineitem/orders local at 4 CN. Confidence high on mechanism; medium (inferred) that the wall gain is ~0.2-0.4 s per query at 4 CN, larger at higher SF (BJ-3).",

21	## Facts established before the analysis
22	1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
23	2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
24	3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
25	4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.
26	
27	## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
28	A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
29	B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
30	C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
31	Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.
32

35	   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
36	6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
37	   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
38	7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
39	   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
40	8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
41	9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
42	10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
43	11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
44	12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).

Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).

48	16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
49	17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
50	18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
51	19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).

4 CN (survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt, card-compare-cn4.txt): the big joins flip to PARTITIONED (shuffle both sides):

Statistics.getOutputSize (Statistics.java:88-108) = sum(type widths) x 1; CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution (cost/CostModel.java:401-432):
BROADCAST cost = outputSize x aliveBackendNumber, SHUFFLE cost = outputSize (x factor). So with N=1 broadcast beats shuffling both sides; with N=4 shuffle wins unless the build side is narrow
(customer c_custkey 4B vs orders 16B -> customer stays BROADCAST). EnforceAndCostTask.checkBroadcastRowCountLimit (task/EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-322) never trips: rowCount 1 <= broadcastRowCountLimit 15,000,000.

## 4. Engine-side re-planning inside the receiver fragment (fact 11 mechanism)

engine.rs:540-585 declares the exact parked row count per stream before build(); stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46 feeds it to DuckDB's TableFunction cardinality callback.
DuckDB join-order (query_graph_manager.cpp:264-266): right child = build = smaller estimated cardinality. DuckDB JoinFilterPushdown pushes build-side filters into PROBE-side scans
(join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:61-134); Sirius wraps the probe leaf (GPU_SCAN or STREAMING_SOURCE) in DYNAMIC_FILTER (sirius_physical_plan_generator.cpp:296-324).
=> DYNAMIC_FILTER on X means X is a probe side.

Translated plans (cn1/cluster.log 'translated StarRocks plan fragment' blocks, lines ~3184 q03, 12533 q10, 14162 q12, 15297 q14, 18958 q19):
- q19 receiver 996c: Join(Filter[p_size<=15 ...](part Read), sirius_stream_3). cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546: STREAMING_SOURCE(4)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(5) 120 tasks 3.66GB -> 0.01GB; HASH_JOIN(9) n=1 in=0.02GB. => build = part (est 203M x 0.2 x 0.2 ~ 8.1M; actual 2.16M), probe = lineitem stream. Engine flipped the FE's build side. Fragment 150 ms.
- q10 receiver 315c: Join(Project(Join(Filter[is_not_null($0)](customer Read), stream_2 nation)), stream_12). cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573: Pipeline 9 [STREAMING_SOURCE(10)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(11)] 17 tasks 2.29GB => the 114.7M-row stream is PROBE; build = customer x nation (150M rows, PARTITION(8) 25.55GB 0.479s, CONCAT(9) 0.114s, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.301s).
  Cause: DuckDB RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2 (duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57, applied .cpp:149) on the FE's null-rejecting scan conjunct (translated by expr_translator.rs:630/929 'is_not_null_pred'): customer 150M x 0.2 = 30M < 114.7M declared. Standalone (no is_not_null) estimates customer x nation 151.5M and has no DYNAMIC_FILTER on the lineitem x orders side.
- q12 receiver 69a: Filter[is_not_null](orders Read) est 1.54B x 0.2 = 308M vs stream 31.2M -> build = stream (sensible). q14 c3: lineitem Read (date filter) 1.22B x 0.2 = 244M vs stream part 200M -> build = part (same as standalone; actual lineitem 75M would be better). q03 a208: lineitem 1.22B x 0.2 = 244M vs stream 145.8M -> build = stream.

## 5. 1-CN timelines (cn1/cluster.log 'fragment run started/finished'), strictly serial per CN

q03.r1: customer 44 ms -> orders x customer 509 ms -> lineitem x stream 2193 ms -> agg 13 -> result 2 (gaps 15/19/3/1 ms). Sum 2761 of 3031 ms reported.
q10.r1: nation 4 -> orders 386 -> lineitem x orders 1753 -> customer x nation x stream 1067 -> agg 179 -> result 5 (sum 3394; gaps ~90 ms).
q12.r1: lineitem 1899 -> orders x stream 405 -> agg 4 -> result 2. q14.r1: part 46 -> lineitem x stream 2330 -> result 4. q19.r1: lineitem 2641 -> part x stream 165 -> result 3.
Engine: one engine thread (engine.rs:242-280 `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`), dispatch worker "Executes ready receiver fragments sequentially" (compute_node_service.rs:376-392).
Parity with standalone within +-13% except q10 (1.2x): the hash-join dependency serialises standalone too; the fragment boundary costs only relay + PARTITION/CONCAT (q03: CONCAT(2) 13 ms on 2.33 GB).

## 6. 4-CN timeline q03.r1 (cluster.log lines 10260-11250), span 1.418 s (Quent), 1639 ms reported

All 16 fragment RPCs arrived 13:19:44.708-44.719 (+ result fragment 44.765). Per CN (times relative to 44.7187):

- drain of 3 remote destinations, SEQUENTIAL, after 'finished': transmits done at +95/+190/+283 ms (each elapsed_ms 93-96, lease_ms 1, write_ms 6-8 = 600-717 GB/s, 4.82-4.89 GB) => ~87 ms of each 95 ms is export_packed_next (engine.rs:813 engine_call -> pack on the engine thread)

cd /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
qid='6293412eec51'
lines=open('cn4/cluster.log',errors='replace').read().splitlines()
ansi=re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m')
ev=[]
for i,l in enumerate(lines[10200:11300],10200):
    s=ansi.sub('',l)
    if qid not in s: continue
    if 'fragment run started' in s or 'fragment run finished' in s or 'transmitted batches via nixl' in s or 'received remote batches' in s or 'declared input stream cardinality' in s:
        ts=s.split()[0]
        m=re.search(r'T(\d\d):(\d\d):(\d\d\.\d+)Z',ts)
        t=int(m.group(1))*3600+int(m.group(2))*60+float(m.group(3))
        kind='start' if 'run started' in s else 'finish' if 'run finished' in s else 'tx' if 'transmitted' in s else 'rx' if 'received remote' in s else 'decl'
        fid=re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=\S*?(\w{4})\b',s)
        fid=re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=[0-9a-f-]+',s); fid=fid.group(0)[-4:] if fid else '?'
        addr=re.search(r'(?:addr|listen|cn|self|node)[a-z_]*=(127\.0\.0\.1:\d+)',s)
        dest=re.search(r'dest=(127\.0\.0\.1:\d+)',s)
        role=re.search(r'role=(\w+)',s)
        ms=re.search(r'elapsed_ms=(\d+)',s)
        byt=re.search(r'bytes=(\d+)',s)
        st=re.search(r'stream_id=(\d+)',s)
        ev.append((t,kind,fid,addr.group(1) if addr else '', dest.group(1) if dest else '', role.group(1) if role else '', ms.group(1) if ms else '', byt.group(1) if byt else '', st.group(1) if st else '', i))
t0=min(e[0] for e in ev)
for e in sorted(ev):
    print(f"{e[0]-t0:7.3f} {e[1]:6} fid={e[2]} {e[3]:16} dest={e[4]:16} role={e[5]:8} ms={e[6]:4} bytes={e[7]:>11} stream={e[8]:2} L{e[9]}")
EOF

import re, json, collections
d=json.load(open('cn4-cnlog.json'))
ansi=re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m')
lines=[ansi.sub('',l) for l in open('cn4/cluster.log',errors='replace')]
def ts(s):
    m=re.search(r'T(\d\d):(\d\d):(\d\d\.\d+)Z',s); return int(m.group(1))*3600+int(m.group(2))*60+float(m.group(3))
for run in ['q03.r1','q10.r1','q12.r1','q19.r1','q14.r1']:
    qid=d[run]['query_ids'][0]
    ev=[]
    for l in lines:
        if qid not in l: continue
        if 'fragment run started' in l or 'fragment run finished' in l or 'transmitted batches via nixl' in l:
            fid=re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=([0-9a-f-]+)',l).group(1)[-4:]
            cn=re.search(r'cn=(127\.0\.0\.1:\d+)',l)
            ev.append((ts(l),'start' if 'started' in l else 'finish' if 'finished' in l else 'tx',fid,cn.group(1) if cn else None,
                       re.search(r'stream_id=(\d+)',l).group(1) if 'stream_id' in l else None, int(re.search(r'bytes=(\d+)',l).group(1)) if 'bytes=' in l else 0))
    ev.sort(); t0=ev[0][0]; span=ev[-1][0]-t0
    fin={}; cnof={}; lasttx=collections.defaultdict(float); txb=collections.Counter(); st={}
    for t,k,f,cn,s,b in ev:
        if k=='start': st[f]=t; cnof[f]=cn
        if k=='finish': fin[f]=t
        if k=='tx' and b>0: lasttx[f]=max(lasttx[f],t); txb[f]+=b; 
    # drain per sender fragment = last tx - finish
    print(f"== {run} span={span:.3f}s reported={d[run]['ms']}ms")
    per_cn=collections.defaultdict(float)
    for f in sorted(fin, key=lambda f: st[f]):
        dr=lasttx[f]-fin[f] if f in lasttx else 0
        if txb[f]>1e8:
            print(f"  frag {f} cn={cnof[f]} start=+{st[f]-t0:.3f} run={fin[f]-st[f]:.3f}s drain={dr:.3f}s tx={txb[f]/1e9:.2f}GB")
            per_cn[cnof[f]]+=dr
    print("  drain sum per CN:", {k:round(v,3) for k,v in per_cn.items()})
EOF

input.corrections:
1. Sub-claim 'at 1 CN every join is BROADCAST' is wrong. survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) has PARTITIONED or BUCKET_SHUFFLE joins in q02 q05 q07 q08 q09 q13 q17 q18 q20 q21 (lines 10, 14, 16, 18, 26, 34, 36, 40, 42); only q03 q04 q10 q11 q12 q14 q15 q16 q19 q22 are all-BROADCAST at 1 CN. Reword to 'for this family (q03/q10/q12/q14/q19) every join is BROADCAST at 1 CN'.

2. Mechanism attribution (evidence item 1, code_refs CostModel.java:401-432). In this cluster the CNs are COMPUTE NODEs (src/lib.rs:211 'ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE'; FE log 'ComputeNode [id=10001..12003]' in survey/cluster.log and cn4/cluster.log). ConnectContext.getAliveBackendNumber() -> SystemInfoService.getAliveBackendNumber() = getBackendIds(true).size() over idToBackendRef only (SystemInfoService.java:1047-1048, 1123-1128; addComputeNode puts into idToComputeNodeRef, :174), so aliveBackendNumber = 0, beNum = 1, and the BROADCAST exchange cost is (cpu 0, mem R, net R) = 3.5R independent of N. The N-scaling that flips q03's orders join comes from HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost (fe-core/.../cost/HashJoinCostModel.java, memCost = rightOutput x beNum where beNum = aliveBE + aliveCN in shared_data mode; the FE runs shared_data per configs/gb200-4gpu/cluster4-numa.sh:231) weighted 2, plus parallelFactor = aliveBE + aliveCN in getCpuCost. With cardinality 1 everywhere this reduces to: broadcast iff probeWidth > buildWidth x (N - 0.25/N); at N=4 q03 lineitem 24 B vs orders x customer 16 B -> 24 < 63 -> shuffle; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> 20 > 15.75 -> broadcast (matches both 4-CN plans). Also note the 1-CN survey was not 'single node' to the FE: four CNs (10001, 11001, 12002, 12003) were registered with one alive, so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode() (SystemInfoService.java:246-248, counts registered not alive) was false and SHUFFLE network cost was charged; that is why broadcast won at 1 CN for this family. The same code paths make checkBroadcastRowCountLimit use beNum = 1 here, not 4.

3. Proposed change outcome. 'Even a row-count-only estimate re-arms checkBroadcastRowCountLimit (15M) ... so q03/q10/q12/q19 would broadcast the filtered small side' is contradicted for q03 and q10: re-arming the guard makes the FE REFUSE to broadcast a >15M-row side unless the probe is >10x larger in bytes. Row-count-only (columns UNKNOWN): q03 build est = max(orders 1.5B x 0.25, customer 150M x 0.25) = 375M rows (StatisticsCalculator.java:1231-1243), probe 1.5B x 24 B = 36 GB < 375M x 16 B x 10 = 60 GB -> pruned at EnforceAndCostTask.java:184/315-320. Exact stats: 145.8M rows, probe 77.6 GB > 23.3 GB passes the guard, but HashJoinCostModel's probe cache penalty (broadcast min(12, ln(145.8M/1e5)) = 7.28 vs shuffle min(3, ...) = 3) gives broadcast ~315 vs shuffle ~286 cost units -> still PARTITIONED. q10 join 13 (lineitem x orders 114.7M rows as build): guard rejects under both (customer x nation 150M x 92 B = 13.8 GB < 22.9 GB). q12 (est 11.7M < 15M) and q19 (part-filtered est a few M) do flip to BROADCAST. Corrected expectation: the FILES() row-count fix alone recovers q12 (23.5 -> 1.5 GB) and q19 (2.75 -> 0.06 GB), ~26 GB of the ~135 GB 'excess'; q03 (60 GB) and q10's customer shuffle (19.2 GB) additionally require raising broadcast_row_count_limit / broadcast_right_table_scale_factor (SessionVariable.java:1833-1836) and neutralising the CPU-cache penalty in HashJoinCostModel (BOTTOM_NUMBER=100000, BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO=12, SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO=3), or moving the decision to the CN. Confidence on the code reading: high; the cost arithmetic is a hand computation (no FE debug log), medium.

4. Impact numbers. Drains as a share of span: q03 0.283-0.287/1.435 = 20%; q10 0.255-0.285/1.478 = 17-19% (finding says 0.24); q12 0.115-0.125/1.081 = 11% (outside the stated 15-25%); q19 4-6%; q14 5%. '0.28 s/CN drain + 0.5 s arena dwell out of a 1.42 s span' double counts: the dwell (frames land +0.71..+1.01 s, consumed +1.30 s) is the receiver waiting for the customer and orders x customer fragments, which are on the critical path in the broadcast plan too; it is a memory-occupancy cost (88% of the 16 GiB arena), not wall time. The alternative plan also has uncosted work the finding omits: each CN must build the full 145.8M-row (2.33 GB) hash table (4x redundant build) and its lineitem scan cannot start until that side is parked (receiver-first rendezvous, fact 2), whereas today the lineitem scan starts at t=0. My critical-path estimate for the broadcast plan is ~1.1-1.2 s vs 1.435 s measured, so the '0.2-0.4 s per query' gain is plausible for q03 but is an inference, and for q19/q14 the gain is ~0.

5. 'The natural plan (the 1-CN shape generalised)' should be labelled as DuckDB's single-node shape, not what a statistics-aware StarRocks FE produces at 4 nodes (see 3).
extra_evidence: Per-CN drain is strictly serial and on the critical path: cn4/cluster.log q03.r1 sender ec5f (127.0.0.1:9102) finished +0.610 s (L10339), transmits complete +0.705/+0.799/+0.893 (L10429, L10571, L10715), next fragment ec5b on 9102 starts +0.893 (L10732); same pattern on 9132 (ec61 finish +0.684, last tx +0.969, ec5d start +0.970).

Each ~4.85 GB frame: elapsed_ms 92-96, lease_ms 1-2, write_ms 6-8 (600-717 GB/s) => ~87 ms of each drain is CPU-side pack/export, not NVLink transfer; the byte volume matters via pack time, not link bandwidth.

4-CN scan fragments alone cost more GPU time than the 1-CN fused scan+join: q03 lineitem senders run 0.610-0.684 s each (4 x = 2.44-2.73 s) vs the 1-CN fused lineitem x stream fragment 2.193 s (cn1-cnlog.txt q03.r1); cn4-quent.txt:788-800 shows GPU_SCAN 2.147-2.443 s summed over 16-17 tasks per CN (127-144 ms/task). Part of the 4-CN efficiency loss (0.48) is per-task scan slowdown, not the shuffle. (inference: contention on the shared parquet source)

Speed-ups (results-ratios.md): join-free q01 2.35x, q06 2.25x; shuffle-heavy q03 1.93x, q10 2.07x, q12 1.96x; but q19 (2.75 GB, 46x 'excess') 2.14x and q13 (13.8 GB shuffle) 2.13x, i.e. below ~5 GB the shuffle has no measurable wall cost.
